submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 silicosis RCT compared hydrogen plus tetrandrine against tetrandrine, so its between-group benefit is a combination-addition effect.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 42250702 enrolled 116 patients with stage II silicosis in a prospective randomized double-blind controlled study comparing tetrandrine monotherapy with hydrogen inhalation plus tetrandrine. The combination arm improved selected pulmonary, inflammatory and symptom outcomes relative to tetrandrine alone. That comparison supports an incremental combination effect and cannot be used to estimate tetrandrine-versus-placebo efficacy or to imply that isolated tetrandrine produced the between-group improvement.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with stage II silicosis receiving tetrandrine alone or tetrandrine plus hydrogen inhalation
submissions.usageContext: Clinical disease-treatment drug evidence; active-comparator design rather than tetrandrine-versus-placebo efficacy
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Both groups received tetrandrine, so the randomized contrast isolates addition of hydrogen rather than the standalone tetrandrine treatment effect.

submissions.findingTextShort: An older silicosis RCT added tetrandrine plus acetylcysteine to routine therapy and does not isolate tetrandrine monotherapy efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 24370303 randomized 96 patients with silicosis to routine therapy alone or routine therapy plus tetrandrine and acetylcysteine. Because the intervention added two active agents together, any between-group clinical signal is combination evidence and cannot be attributed solely to tetrandrine. The disease-treatment regimen also cannot be converted into consumer supplement dosing guidance.
submissions.populationContext: Patients with silicosis receiving routine care with or without added tetrandrine plus acetylcysteine
submissions.usageContext: Combination clinical-drug evidence, not isolated tetrandrine monotherapy and not consumer supplementation
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Co-intervention with acetylcysteine prevents clean attribution of clinical outcomes to tetrandrine alone.

submissions.findingTextShort: Tetrandrine silicosis regimens are disease-treatment drug protocols and must not become generic supplement dosing guidance.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The human tetrandrine literature identified here concerns structured treatment of silicosis using tetrandrine as a clinical drug, often with active comparators or co-interventions. Study regimens are therefore protocol descriptors, not evidence for a generic consumer dose, wellness use, botanical Fang Ji substitution, or safety across unsupervised oral products. Drug-level tetrandrine and botanical products that may contain tetrandrine or adulterants require separate identity and safety propositions.
submissions.populationContext: Patients with silicosis treated in clinical protocols
submissions.usageContext: Clinical-drug versus consumer-supplement and botanical-product firewall
submissions.safetyContext: Disease-treatment protocols do not establish general consumer safety or interchangeability with Stephania/Fang Ji products.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Route, formulation, co-interventions and clinical monitoring are part of the evidence boundary and prevent generic dosing inheritance.
